To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the breeding performance of a forest-dwelling bird of prey, the northern goshaw (Accipiter gentialis), is best explained by the amount of old spruces and water within a 20000m radius of the nest, while the breeding performance of two other species, the common buzzard (Butao buteo) and the European honey buzzard(Pernis apivora), is not associated with the habitat around their nests.

breeding success of goshawk (a species that has declined in Finland) is best explained by the proportion of old spruce and water, and the proportion of young thinning within a 20000-m radius around the nest, while breeding success of common buzzard (a species that is increasing in Finland) is not explained by the habitat variables.

breeding success of northern goshawk was more successful with old spruce forest, water and less young thinning forest within a 2002-m radius around nests, but the habitat requirements of common buzzard and European honey buzzards were different from those of northern goshawks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the habitat effects on the breeding performance of three forest-dwelling hawks in Finland.
the effects of forestry on forest-dwelling birds of prey.
the effects of forest management on the breeding performance of three raptor species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
old forest is important for the breeding performance of the goshaw, but not for the common buzzard and the European honey buzzard.
the old forest specialist species are not doing well in the current Finnish forests, and that the situation is not likely to improve in the near future.
the breeding performance of forest-dwelling species may be affected by the loss of old forest habitats, although the effects are species-specific and may vary with the distance from the nest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the boreal forests are changing, but the effects of this change on the breeding performance of forest-dwelling hawks is not yet known.
the breeding habitat of the goshawks is more restricted than previously thought, and that the amount of old forest has decreased in the southern Finland during 1992–2009.
old forest habitat is important for the goshawk, and the area of old spruce is declining, which may explain why the goshawk is declining in Finland and elsewhere in the boreal zone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the breeding success of a forest-dwelling hawk species is associated with old spruce forest, and that old spruce forest is declining in Finland.
the habitat requirements of the goshawks are not met in the southern boreal forest, and that their breeding success is declining in this area.
the habitat requirements and breeding performance of the goshawks, common buzzards and honey buzzards are best explained at a 2-km radius around the nests.
